text:
The fix is straightforward. The original `slugify` only replaced non-alphanumeric characters with hyphens, but didn't handle consecutive hyphens or leading/trailing hyphens. I added two lines:

1. `re.sub(r"-+", "-", text)` — collapses multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.
2. `text.strip("-")` — removes any leading or trailing hyphens.

This ensures `"Hello,  World!"` → `"hello-world"` and `"--a--b--"` → `"a-b"`.

arguments.summary: Fixed slugify in textkit/slug.py by adding two post-processing steps: collapsing consecutive hyphens with re.sub(r"-+", "-", text) and stripping leading/trailing hyphens with text.strip("-"). This ensures the function returns a clean slug with single hyphens and no surrounding hyphens.
